derivation: Generated by tools/import_kicad_board.py from the vendor's own KiCad footprint. Pad centres are exact to three decimal places in millimetres, scaled at 8.0 px/mm from a 25.24 x 20.16 mm extent including a 1.0 mm margin. Pin names joined from the symbol library on pad number. Nothing here was measured off an image.
assumption: Every `pin` is null: that field is the rcontrol pin index of a PICSimLab board implementation (webui/pinmap.py), and none exists for this board. `chip_pin` and `chip_index` are what tools/import_pindefs.py read out of the board-support packages named in `pindefs`; a pad whose `chip_pin` is null says why in `why_null`. No board module describes nRF54L15 here, so no level is read for any pad and the pin view reports every one as not modelled until a module and a core exist; `chip_pin` is recorded so that the join is ready, not made. 18 pins on this board are named with NO flat number -- P2.08, P1.11, P1.10, and so on -- so every pad reaching one carries `chip_index` null for that reason and not for a missing reading: no flat GPIO numbering is published for the nRF54L15 at all, so a module for it would key its own table the way webui/boards/samd21.py does, and until one exists no level is read for any pad here.

pindefs.derivation: Generated by tools/import_pindefs.py from the board-support packages in `packages`, at those revisions. Nothing was inferred from the CAD, the silkscreen or a pinout image: a label resolves only when every package covering the board that defines it names the same pin, and `python tools/import_pindefs.py <board>` prints the file that named it.

pads.label: SAMD11_SWDIO
pads.why_null: this pad reaches the on-board debugger, an ATSAMD11D14A, and not this board's own MCU; `chip_pin` names a pin of the board's MCU, so a number here would be a pin of the wrong chip. Seeed's own board file names both parts, and the debugger's pins are reachable from it if they are ever wanted under a field that says which chip it means
